newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo gains after chief exec presentation.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo gains after chief exec presentation.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc rose on Wednesday, echoing gains in the drug company's ADRs in New York, after a well-received presentation to a U.S. conference by chief executive Richard Sykes, dealers said.
Glaxo shares were up 16-1/2p, or 1.3 percent, at 12.89-1/2 stg by 0836 GMT, in volume of 1.1 million shares, after the ADRs rose $1 to $41-1/2.
Market sources said Sykes addressed some 150 institutional fund managers at a global healthcare conference in California organised by Goldman Sachs.
They said his comments were based on a recent Glaxo research and development briefing, though further detail was not immediately available.
"There has been some very strong U.S. buying in Glaxo after the presentation," said one dealer.
A Glaxo spokesman confirmed Sykes had addressed the meeting, adding that his comments had focused on Glaxo's R&D bulletin issued on May 2.

Sykes' comments included prospective new drug launches, the broad spread of therapeutic areas that the company was operating in, new products for HIV and prospects for growth in demand for migraine treatments, and other issues, the spokesman said.
